title: COMET: Towards Practical W4A4KV4 LLMs Serving
problem: Prevalent LLM quantization methods (W8A8 or W4-only) do not fully utilize INT4 tensor cores on modern GPUs and cannot reduce the KV cache memory bottleneck, because quantizing activations to 4-bit causes unacceptable accuracy loss with standard methods, leaving W4A4 impractical.
motivation: LLM inference is bottlenecked by GPU memory bandwidth and capacity; W4A4KV4 would halve memory traffic versus W8A8 and quarter versus FP16, but requires solving the activation quantization accuracy problem to be practically deployable.
method: COMET introduces a fine-grained mixed-precision quantization algorithm (FMPQ) that compresses most activations to 4-bit while preserving accuracy by identifying and retaining outlier activations at higher precision (e.g., 8-bit) in a mixed-precision format. On the hardware side, COMET develops a highly optimized W4Ax GPU kernel (supporting both W4A4 and W4A8 mixed-precision GEMM) with a novel mixed-precision data layout that co-locates 4-bit and 8-bit activation elements to enable fast dequantization. The kernel uses GPU software pipelining to overlap data loading and conversion with computation, and introduces fine-grained streaming multiprocessor (SM) scheduling to achieve load balance across SMs. COMET integrates this kernel into a full LLM inference framework with efficient KV4 cache management supporting models like LLaMA-3-70B on a single A100-80G.
key_novelty: Fine-grained mixed-precision quantization (FMPQ) enabling practical W4A4 by selectively retaining outlier activations at INT8, combined with a W4Ax kernel with mixed-precision data layout and SM-level load-balanced scheduling to fully exploit INT4 tensor cores.
contributions: FMPQ: fine-grained mixed-precision quantization algorithm compressing most activations to INT4 with negligible accuracy loss
Optimized W4Ax kernel with mixed-precision data layout for fast dequantization and software pipelining
Fine-grained SM scheduling achieving load balance across streaming multiprocessors
COMET inference framework: first practical W4A4KV4 LLM serving system with 2.88x kernel speedup over cuBLAS and 2.02x end-to-end throughput over TensorRT-LLM

metrics.speedup: 2.88x kernel-level speedup over cuBLAS; 2.02x end-to-end throughput vs TensorRT-LLM on A100-80G
metrics.accuracy: negligible accuracy loss vs FP16 for LLaMA family models
metrics.other: evaluated on LLaMA-3-70B on single A100-80G-SMX4

limitations: Mixed-precision overhead for outlier activations adds complexity; KV4 accuracy impact on long-context or specialized LLM tasks not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: practical W4A4KV4 LLM inference via fine-grained mixed-precision quantization
